note.text:
Density is the mass of each unit of volume: density = mass ÷ volume.
Units: g/cm³ or kg/m³ (the SI unit). 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³.
To find the density of a stone: measure its mass with a balance and its volume by displacement, then divide.
The density of water is 1 g/cm³. A body less dense than water floats; a body more dense than water sinks. Some densities: ice about 0.92 g/cm³ (it floats), kerosene about 0.8 g/cm³, iron about 7.9 g/cm³ (it sinks).
Two bodies of the same size can have different masses because their densities are different: a block of iron is much heavier than a block of wood of the same size.

worked_example.problem: A metal block has a mass of {m} g and a volume of {v} cm³. What is its density? Will it float in water?
steps: Water is {w} g/cm³. {density(m, v)} is more than {w}, so the block sinks.

cards.idea: Density = mass ÷ volume. It tells how much mass is packed into each cm³.
Water has a density of 1 g/cm³. Less dense than water: it floats. More dense: it sinks.
example: Wood (about {w} g/cm³) floats. Iron (about {i} g/cm³) sinks.

check.prompt: A block has a density of {d} g/cm³. Will it float or sink in water?

misconceptions.explain: Compare with water, 1 g/cm³: less than 1 floats, more than 1 sinks.

solution: {d} g/cm³ is {floatsInWater(d) ? 'less' : 'more'} than the density of water.

cards.idea: Units of density: g/cm³ or kg/m³. 1 g/cm³ = {convertUnit(1, 'kg', 'g')} kg/m³.

questions.prompt: A block has a mass of {d * v} g and a volume of {v} cm³. What is its density?

misconceptions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume: divide, do not multiply.
Divide the mass by the volume, not the volume by the mass.

questions.prompt: A stone has a density of {d} g/cm³ and a volume of {v} cm³. What is its mass?
A block has a mass of {d * v} g and a volume of {v} cm³. Will it float or sink in water?

misconceptions.explain: Work out the density (mass ÷ volume) and compare it with water, 1 g/cm³.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Ice floats because it is less dense than water.
A body denser than water sinks.

wrong.text: A big log sinks because it is heavy.
wrong.explain: Size does not decide: wood floats because its density is less than water's.
Iron (about 7.9 g/cm³) is denser than water: it sinks.
